memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for initial consultation with Dr Nandini Kulkarni (Geriatric Medicine) on 2025-04-15 at 10:00 am. Reason: review of hypothyroidism, dyslipidaemia and allergic rhinitis. Patient to bring recent labs if available.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
levothyroxine 50 mcg OD
atorvastatin 10 mg HS
cetirizine 10 mg HS

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling more tired than usual and my nose is constantly blocked, especially in the mornings. I also notice mild weight gain despite my usual diet. My sleep is okay but I wake up feeling unrefreshed.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports mild fatigue, no difficulty with ADLs; continues full-time work as electrician.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 4/5 (negative), no need for further assessment.
falls: zero falls in last 12 months; gait normal; timed up-and-go 9 seconds (within normal).
medicines: 3 regular (levothyroxine 50 mcg OD, atorvastatin 10 mg HS, cetirizine 10 mg HS); polypharmacy not applicable.
mood: denies depression or anxiety; reports occasional irritability.
carers: wife (Spouse) supportive.
goals: "I want to have more energy to keep up with my work and feel less congested."

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Skin prick test: positive reaction to house dust mite (3+ wheal), grass pollen (2+), negative to cat dander. Consistent with allergic rhinitis.

cognition: Mini-Cog not repeated (annual screen due).

medicines: 5 regular (levothyroxine 75 mcg, atorvastatin 10 mg HS, cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray, montelukast 10 mg HS); polypharmacy present – request medication review per Beers criteria.

carers: wife (Spouse).

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Referral to ENT specialist (Dr S. Rao) for persistent allergic rhinitis despite intranasal steroid and antihistamine. Request skin prick testing and consideration of immunotherapy.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: ENT reply: Skin prick test confirms dust mite allergy. Recommends continuation of current pharmacotherapy and offers sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) after 3 months. No surgical intervention needed.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: My nasal congestion has improved a lot since starting the nasal spray and montelukast. I still get occasional itchy eyes but overall I feel better. Energy levels are decent; I can manage my work shifts without needing naps.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports good stamina; able to complete full workday without fatigue.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 3/5 (negative) – annual screen passed.
falls: zero falls; gait normal; timed up-and-go 8 seconds.
medicines: 5 regular (levothyroxine 100 mcg OD, rosuvastatin 10 mg OD, cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray, montelukast 10 mg HS); polypharmacy present – medication review per Beers criteria scheduled.
mood: denies depression; reports occasional stress related to work.
carers: wife (Spouse).
goals: "I want to maintain this level of energy and keep my allergies under control."
